task.title: Plan the design for a coaching centre's admission flyer
task.brief: Read the client brief in the material below. In 15 to 20 minutes, write a short design plan (no drawing needed). A good answer covers: the main message and what readers should see first, a simple layout (what goes top, middle, bottom), colours and fonts with a reason, the print specs you will use (size, bleed, colour mode, resolution), the extra versions you will make for WhatsApp and Instagram, and 2 or 3 questions you would ask the client before starting. Use plain words and bullet points.
task.material:
Client: Bright Path Coaching, Vijayawada.
Need: A5 flyer to hand out at schools, plus versions for WhatsApp and Instagram.
Content: New batches for Class 10 and Intermediate (MPC, BiPC). Starts 1 June. 20% early-bird fee discount till 15 May. Free demo class every Sunday. Phone: 90000 00000. Address: 2nd floor, near bus stand.
Client wishes: 'Put everything big. Use lots of colours. Add photos of all 12 teachers. Logo is a JPG from our old website.'
Budget: printing 5,000 copies on 130 gsm paper.
key_points: Picks one main message (new batches or early-bird discount) as the focal point
Clear layout with hierarchy, not everything big
Limited colour palette and at most two fonts, with reasons
Print specs: A5 (148 x 210 mm), about 3 mm bleed, CMYK, 300 dpi
Notes the JPG logo may be low quality and asks for a vector or redraws it
Suggests a better option than 12 teacher photos (few photos or a group photo)
Separate sizes for WhatsApp and Instagram (for example 1080 x 1080 and Story 1080 x 1920)
Asks sensible client questions (brand colours, photo quality, deadline)

rubric.label: Technical correctness
rubric.guide: 0 = wrong or no print/digital specs, 3 = some specs right, 5 = size, bleed, CMYK, dpi and digital sizes all correct

rubric.label: Design thinking
rubric.guide: 0 = follows 'everything big' blindly, 3 = some hierarchy, 5 = clear focal point, layout and reasons that suit parents and students

rubric.label: Client handling
rubric.guide: 0 = ignores weak inputs, 3 = notes some issues, 5 = politely flags logo and photo issues and asks good questions

rubric.label: Clarity
rubric.guide: 0 = hard to follow, 3 = understandable, 5 = short, organised bullets anyone can follow
